Update Header Statistics

Source: R/update_header_stats.R
update_header_stats.Rd


Use this function to update the statistics that can be injected into gtsummary table headers with modify_header(), e.g. {N}, {n}, {p}, and {level}. This is useful, for example, when the headers should report population Ns that differ from the Ns in the data summarized in the table.

  • Tables with a by variable (columns 'stat_1', 'stat_2', etc.): pass a univariate tabulation of the by variable, e.g. cards::ard_tabulate(variables = trt). The levels of the tabulated variable are matched by position to the 'stat_1', 'stat_2', etc. columns. If the table also includes an overall 'stat_0' column (e.g. from add_overall()), its statistics are updated with the total N from the tabulation.

  • Tables without a by variable (a single 'stat_0' column): pass the total N, e.g. cards::ard_total_n().

Statistics are glued into the headers when modify_header() is called. Therefore, after updating the statistics, you must call modify_header() to see the updated numbers in the table.

Usage

update_header_stats(x, card)

Arguments

x

(gtsummary)
Object with class 'gtsummary'

card

(card)
Object of class 'card'. Either a univariate tabulation, typically created with cards::ard_tabulate(), or the total N, typically created with cards::ard_total_n(). See details above.

Value

gtsummary object

Examples

# Example 1 ----------------------------------
tbl_summary(trial, by = trt, include = age) |>
  update_header_stats(
    # doubling the trial data set and the Ns
    card =
      rbind(trial, trial) |>
      cards::ard_tabulate(variables = trt)
  ) |>
  modify_header(all_stat_cols() ~ "**{level}**  \n N = {n}")
#> ! You must update the headers to utilize the updated numbers.
#> ℹ For example, `modify_header(all_stat_cols() ~ '**{level}**, N = {n}')`

# Example 2 ----------------------------------
tbl_summary(trial, include = age) |>
  update_header_stats(
    card = cards::ard_total_n(rbind(trial, trial))
  ) |>
  modify_header(stat_0 ~ "**Overall**  \n N = {N}")
#> ! You must update the headers to utilize the updated numbers.
#> ℹ For example, `modify_header(all_stat_cols() ~ '**{level}**, N = {n}')`
